newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Latvia may join NATO later.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Latvia may join NATO later.

text.p: A day after the United States said it wanted only the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland to be NATO's first new members, it told the Baltic state of Latvia on Friday it stood a chance of joining later.
"Our goal is an integrated Europe. That goal embraces Latvia," Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said before talks with Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs.

"NATO cannot advance promises of membership but we are committed to a process that will help all aspiring nations understand what they must do to make membership a possibility," Albright told reporters.
"We have made it clear that NATO will remain open to all European democracies that are able to contribute to its goals," she added.

Although Latvia and its Baltic neighbours were not named by the White House on Thursday as first-stage candidates for NATO membership, Birkavs expressed his country's appreciation of the U.S. announcement.
"We fully support this major step in a process that has to remain, and we are sure will remain, inclusive," he said.

It became clear at an early stage of the NATO expansion debate that the Baltic states, all former Soviet republics, could not be included in the first wave of new members if Russia was to acquiesce in the move.
But Birkavs said Latvia "firmly believe(s) that NATO enlargement will not be complete until the Baltic states ... are members of the alliance."
He said that already during his visit to Washington he had felt support for his country's aspirations both from members of the U.S. administration and from Congress.

Birkavs noted that Albright had recently said next month's NATO summit, which will invite membership applications from first-wave candidates, was "not a once-a-lifetime event like the arrival of the Hale-Bopp comet".

"Let me express a hope that the NATO enlargement process will be more like the Olympic Games, whose main principle is not to be first but to participate, and of which the cycle is not 3,000 years but two or four years," he said.
Albright said the reason why hopefuls Romania and Slovenia had not been included in Thursday's announcement was the need to maintain consensus in NATO on the countries to be admitted.
Asked about Slovenia, she said: "This is not an anti-Slovenian move, this is a move in order to make sure that NATO remains strong and cohesive."
